cohort: 1528 nulliparous women with uncomplicated pregnancies who gave birth between January 2018 and February 2020 at one academic medical center
finding: Elective IOL at 39.0 weeks' gestation or later was not associated with lower cesarean birth rates compared to expectant management in nulliparous women with uncomplicated pregnancies.
mod_finding: Elective induction of labor was not associated with a statistically significant difference in cesarean birth rates compared to expectant management.
